answers.explanation: Laptops, phones, and access points all transmit and receive. Nothing physically joins them, so they share the air with every radio in range.
Chapter 2's rule of thumb: lower frequencies travel farther and get through obstacles better. The price is fewer channels and a crowded band.
Wired links give stable, guaranteed performance and are harder to eavesdrop on. That's exactly what a data center needs.
Encryption hides what's said, not that something was said. Timing and volume can reveal a lot.
Pulling cable through walls is expensive. Once it's in, it needs little attention. Wireless is cheap to install but needs ongoing tuning and upgrades.
A switch port is a physical location. A radio signal could have come from anywhere in range, including the parking lot.
Everyone on a channel shares it, and interference from other radios makes speed vary.
Mobility is where wireless shines. The other three need throughput and stability, so they're wired.
Access points at the edge bridge the radio side onto the wired core.
